newsitem.title: UK: Roche says Neupogen syringe approved in EU.
newsitem.headline: Roche says Neupogen syringe approved in EU.

text.p: Hoffmann-La Roche said on Wednesday that a syringe formation of cancer treatment Neupogen had been approved for sale in the European Union.

In a statement the Roche Holdings AG unit said the ready-prepared syringe version of the drug was much simpler and quicker to use than existing vials and could lead to more patients being treated at home.

Hoffmann-La Roche has a co-marketing agreement for Neupogen, which was developed by Amgen Inc of the U.S. It is the most widely used drug for stimulating the production of white blood cells, which are a key element in the body's ability to fight infection.
The company said the ready-filled syringe version of the drug had been approved by Britain's Medicine's Control Agency (MCA). Britain was acting as the reference member state for approval in the EU.
Product launches in individual member states will follow the issuing of local licenses, Hoffmann La Roche said.
